newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia slaps anti-dumping duties on paper firms.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia slaps anti-dumping duties on paper firms.

text.p: The Malaysian government said on Friday it had imposed provisional anti-dumping duties on selected European and Indonesian exporters of carbonless, self-copying paper.

A statement issued by Malaysia's Ministry of Trade and Industry on Friday said it had conducted preliminary investigations into allegations by two Malaysian companies that cheap imports of self-copying paper were affecting their profits.

Gamuda Paper Sdn Bhd, a unit of Gamuda Bhd, and Ann Bee (M) Sdn Bhd had filed a petition with the ministry alleging that imports of self-copying paper rolls and sheets from the European Union and Indonesia were at dumped prices and "had caused, or threatened to cause, material injury to the domestic industry producing the like product", the statement said.

The companies listed by the ministry as being affected by the duties are U.K.-based Arjo Wiggins Carbonless Papers International Ltd a unit of Arjo Wiggins Appleton plc ; Germany's Stora Carbonless Paper GmBH; Spain's Torraspapel S.A. and Copyright S.A.; Indonesia's P.T. Parisando Pratama and P.T. Toyolamo.

The duties imposed on the companies range from nine to 39 percent, and would be "effective for not more than 120 days from the date the government gazettes the affirmation (of the) preliminary determination of the investigation", the ministry said.
Ministry spokesman was not available for further details.
The Customs Department would be enforcing the application of the provisional anti-dumping duties, the statement said.
